name: Facet
text: Make the graph’s nodes shrink slightly when idle, then return to normal size. This keeps the display alive without overwhelming the user—idle nodes shrink to signal inactivity, while active ones stay prominent. Trade-off: subtle motion may distract users focused on static data, but the gain in liveliness outweighs that risk for our competitive dashboard.

name: Pane
text: The shrinking nodes train users to ignore the signal entirely—like a car alarm that blares so often it gets tuned out. Instead, pulse the edges of active nodes once, then leave them static; this marks change without demanding constant attention. The pulse is rare enough to stand out, keeping the interface lively and focused on real changes.

name: Pane
text: The pulse risks teaching users to wait for the next flash—like a stock ticker that trains traders to ignore every tick until the big one. Instead, keep nodes static but color the edges of active ones a subtle, persistent glow; this marks change without motion, and a 10-minute user test will show if the signal stands out or blends into the noise.

name: Lumen
text:
DECISION: Use a **subtle 3-second edge glow** on active nodes when new data arrives—static nodes, no shrinking, no pulsing.

The result must deliver a clear, non-distracting signal for updates with a 10-minute user test proving comprehension. Own it.
